data.description:
## What

Cut the emit-side surfaces over to `[non-codebase]`, teaching the recognition-side surfaces to
accept the legacy spelling without documenting it.

CUTOVER (emit): `plan_review_E2.md:12`, `plan_review_E6.md:12`, `plan_review_F1.md:10`,
`coach_moves.py` move 14 (comment + template).
COMPATIBILITY (recognize both): `completion_verifier.md`, `plan_review_evidence_kind.md`,
`plan_review_ac_process_gate.md`, `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md`
(its SCOPE clause gates whether the criterion applies at all), the eval-spec fixtures.

## Why this is ONE commit

Three gates are coupled to this text and all fail if split:
1. `tests/unit/test_measurement_provenance_criterion.py` pins SHA256 digests AND exact line
   counts for five files. Its `_contract_lines()` selector keeps lines containing
   `"OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE"` or `"[operator-attested]"` — cut over without widening the
   SELECTOR and it matches ZERO lines, failing with a misleading
   "expected 1 contract line(s), found 0".
2. `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is generated from these prompts and gated by
   `registry.validate_criteria_guide(...) == []` in five test files plus content pins in
   `tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py`.
3. The `reviewers/index.json` drift gate fires on any front-matter change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Emit-side prompts and coach move 14 instruct `[non-codebase]`.
- [ ] Recognition-side prompts state that the legacy spelling is still accepted.
- [ ] `_contract_lines()` selects the new text; digests and counts are recomputed in this commit.
- [ ] `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` run and committed;
      `validate_criteria_guide` returns `[]`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
data.title: S4 — cut prompts, coach text and the generated guide over to [non-codebase]
